Return `True` if the call was successfully cancelled or finished
running.

result(timeout=None)¶

Return the value returned by the call. If the call hasn’t yet completed
then this method will wait up to timeout seconds. If the call hasn’t
completed in timeout seconds, then a
`TimeoutError` will be raised. timeout can be
an int or float. If timeout is not specified or `None`, there is no
limit to the wait time.

If the future is cancelled before completing then `CancelledError`
will be raised.

If the call raised an exception, this method will raise the same exception.

exception(timeout=None)¶

Return the exception raised by the call. If the call hasn’t yet
completed then this method will wait up to timeout seconds. If the
call hasn’t completed in timeout seconds, then a
`TimeoutError` will be raised. timeout can be
an int or float. If timeout is not specified or `None`, there is no
limit to the wait time.

If the future is cancelled before completing then `CancelledError`
will be raised.

If the call completed without raising, `None` is returned.

add_done_callback(fn)¶

Attaches the callable fn to the future. fn will be called, with the
future as its only argument, when the future is cancelled or finishes
running.

Added callables are called in the order that they were added and are
always called in a thread belonging to the process that added them. If
the callable raises an `Exception` subclass, it will be logged and
ignored. If the callable raises a `BaseException` subclass, the
behavior is undefined.

If the future has already completed or been cancelled, fn will be
called immediately.

The following `Future` methods are meant for use in unit tests and
`Executor` implementations.

set_running_or_notify_cancel()¶

This method should only be called by `Executor` implementations
before executing the work associated with the `Future` and by unit
tests.

If the method returns `False` then the `Future` was cancelled,
i.e. `Future.cancel()` was called and returned `True`. Any threads
waiting on the `Future` completing (i.e. through
`as_completed()` or `wait()`) will be woken up.

If the method returns `True` then the `Future` was not cancelled
and has been put in the running state, i.e. calls to
`Future.running()` will return `True`.

skill_drafts.name: Future Result Retrieval with Timeout
skill_drafts.description: Retrieve the result of a completed asynchronous task, with optional timeout enforcement and exception propagation. Use when a caller needs the output of a parallel task and must handle timeout or cancellation states.
skill_drafts.objective: Safely retrieve result from a Future object with timeout and error handling
applicable_signals: Future object is available and in a completed or running state
Caller has a timeout requirement or can tolerate indefinite wait
Result value is needed for downstream processing
contraindications: The future has not been submitted to an executor yet
The caller does not need the result and can proceed without it
The task is still being configured and has not started running
workflow_steps: Obtain a Future object from an executor's submit() or map() call
Call future.result(timeout=<seconds>) or future.result() with no timeout
Handle TimeoutError if timeout is specified and elapsed
Handle CancelledError if the future was cancelled before completion
Catch and handle any exception raised by the underlying task
Use the returned value for downstream processing
triggers: A parallel task submitted to ThreadPoolExecutor or ProcessPoolExecutor has completed or is expected to complete
The caller needs the return value of an asynchronous task
A maximum wait time must be enforced before raising TimeoutError
constraints: timeout parameter must be int, float, or None
If timeout is specified and elapsed, TimeoutError is raised
If future was cancelled before completion, CancelledError is raised
If the underlying task raised an exception, that exception is propagated
cautions: Blocking call: result() will block the calling thread until the task completes or timeout expires
Exception propagation: any exception raised by the task will be re-raised by result()
Timeout precision: timeout is a best-effort limit; actual wait may vary slightly
output_contract: Returns the value returned by the completed call. If the call has not completed within the timeout period, raises TimeoutError. If the future was cancelled, raises CancelledError. If the call raised an exception, that exception is re-raised. If no exception occurred and the call completed, the return value is guaranteed to be available.

examples.input: future = executor.submit(some_function, arg1, arg2); result = future.result(timeout=5)
examples.output: Returns the return value of some_function(arg1, arg2) if it completes within 5 seconds; raises TimeoutError if it does not.
examples.notes: Typical use case with timeout enforcement

examples.output: Re-raises the exception that failing_function raised during execution

metadata.prompt: Call result(timeout=None) on a Future object to retrieve the return value of the completed task. If timeout is specified (int or float), the method will wait up to that many seconds; if the task has not completed by then, TimeoutError is raised. If the future was cancelled before completion, CancelledError is raised. If the task raised an exception, that same exception is re-raised by this method. If timeout is None or omitted, there is no limit to the wait time.

skill_drafts.name: Future Exception Inspection with Timeout
skill_drafts.description: Retrieve the exception raised by a completed asynchronous task, with optional timeout enforcement. Use when a caller needs to inspect what error occurred in a parallel task without re-raising it.
skill_drafts.objective: Safely inspect exception from a Future object with timeout and cancellation handling
applicable_signals: Caller needs to examine exception without propagating it
Error handling decision required based on exception type
contraindications: Future has not been submitted to executor
Caller intends to re-raise the exception (use result() instead)
Task is still running and caller cannot wait
Timeout value is negative or invalid
intervention_moves: Call future.exception(timeout) to retrieve exception object
Check if returned value is None (no exception) or an exception instance
Handle TimeoutError if timeout expires before completion
Handle CancelledError if future was cancelled
triggers: A parallel task has completed and the caller needs to examine what exception (if any) was raised, without propagating it immediately.
constraints: timeout parameter must be int, float, or None
If timeout is None, wait indefinitely
Method must be called on a Future object from concurrent.futures
Callable must be invoked in a thread belonging to the process that added it
cautions: If future is already completed or cancelled, exception() returns immediately
TimeoutError is raised if timeout expires before completion
CancelledError is raised if future was cancelled before completion
Returned exception is the actual exception object, not a string or wrapper
output_contract: Returns the exception object raised by the call, or None if the call completed without raising; raises TimeoutError if timeout expires before completion; raises CancelledError if future was cancelled.

examples.notes: Waits up to 5 seconds for task completion, then returns exception or None

metadata.prompt: Call exception(timeout=None) on a Future object to retrieve the exception raised by the task. If timeout is specified (int or float), wait up to that many seconds; if the task has not completed by then, TimeoutError is raised. If the future was cancelled, CancelledError is raised. If the task completed without raising an exception, None is returned. If the task raised an exception, that exception object is returned (not re-raised).

skill_drafts.name: Future Completion Callback Registration
skill_drafts.description: Attach a callable to be invoked when a Future completes or is cancelled. Use when a caller needs to trigger side effects (logging, cleanup, chaining) upon task completion without blocking.
skill_drafts.objective: Register a non-blocking callback to execute when a Future transitions to done or cancelled state
applicable_signals: A parallel task has been submitted and wrapped in a Future
The caller needs to perform an action upon task completion without synchronous blocking
Side effects such as logging, state updates, or chaining to the next task are required
contraindications: Do not use if the caller needs the result value; use result() or exception() instead
Do not use if the callback must raise exceptions and have them propagated; exceptions are logged and ignored
Do not use if the callback must execute in a specific thread other than the submitting process thread
intervention_moves: Define a callable fn that accepts a single Future argument
Call future.add_done_callback(fn) to register the callback
Verify the callback is invoked after the Future completes or is cancelled
triggers: A parallel task is submitted and the caller needs to perform an action (e.g., log, update state, trigger next task) as soon as it completes, without waiting synchronously.
constraints: The callback receives only the Future object as its argument
Exceptions raised by the callable are logged and ignored; BaseException subclasses have undefined behavior
Callables are always executed in a thread belonging to the process that added them
If the Future is already completed or cancelled when add_done_callback is called, fn is invoked immediately
cautions: Do not rely on exception propagation from the callback; use logging or side effects instead
Ensure the callback is lightweight to avoid blocking other callbacks or the executor thread
If multiple callbacks are registered, they execute in registration order
output_contract: The callback is registered and will be invoked with the Future as its sole argument upon completion or cancellation. add_done_callback itself returns None and does not block.

metadata.prompt: Call add_done_callback(fn) on a Future object to register a callable fn. The callable will be invoked exactly once when the Future is cancelled or finishes running, with the Future as its only argument. Callables are invoked in the order they were added, always in a thread belonging to the process that added them. If the Future has already completed or been cancelled, fn will be called immediately. Exceptions raised by the callable are logged and ignored; BaseException subclasses have undefined behavior.

skill_drafts.name: Future Cancellation Status Check
skill_drafts.description: Query whether a Future was successfully cancelled or has finished running without blocking. Use when a caller needs to determine if a task can still be cancelled or has already completed.
skill_drafts.objective: Query the cancellation and completion state of a Future without blocking
applicable_signals: Caller does not need to wait for task completion
Caller does not need the actual result or exception value
contraindications: Caller needs the actual result value (use result() instead)
Caller needs the exception raised by the task (use exception() instead)
Caller is inside an Executor implementation (use set_running_or_notify_cancel() instead)
Caller needs to register a completion callback (use add_done_callback() instead)
workflow_steps: Obtain a Future object from an Executor (ThreadPoolExecutor or ProcessPoolExecutor)
Receive boolean result: True if cancelled or finished, False otherwise
Use result to decide next action (e.g., retry, wait, or proceed)
triggers: Caller needs to determine if a submitted task can still be cancelled
Caller needs to check if a task has already finished (successfully or with exception)
Non-blocking state inspection is required before deciding on next action
constraints: Must be called on a valid Future object
Returns immediately without waiting for task completion
Does not retrieve or raise exceptions from the task
cautions: Return value True means either cancelled OR finished; caller must use other methods to distinguish between the two states if needed
State may change immediately after this call returns if task is still running
output_contract: Returns boolean True if the Future was successfully cancelled or has finished running; returns False if the Future is still running and cancellation was not possible.

metadata.prompt: Call cancel() on a Future object to check its cancellation and completion state. This method returns True if the Future was cancelled or finished running, False otherwise. It does not block and does not retrieve the result or exception.
